title: D. Satyam and Counting
statement:
Satyam is given n distinct points on the 2D coordinate plane. It is guaranteed that 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all given points (x_i, y_i). How many different nondegenerate right triangles^{∗} can be formed from choosing three different points as its vertices?

Two triangles a and b are different if there is a point v such that v is a vertex of a but not a vertex of b.

^{∗}A nondegenerate right triangle has positive area and an interior 90^circ angle.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) — the number of points.

The following n lines contain two integers x_i and y_i (0 ≤ x_i ≤ n, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1) — the i'th point that Satyam can choose from. It is guaranteed that all (x_i, y_i) are pairwise distinct.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

Output an integer for each test case, the number of distinct nondegenerate right triangles that can be formed from choosing three points.

The four triangles in question for the first test case:

Input:
```
351 01 13 05 02 130 01 03 091 02 03 04 05 02 17 18 19 1
```

Output:
```
4
0
8
```
